title: Capacity Hedging: Rolling Runway & Scope Auction for Cross-Initiative Conflicts
creator: Ava Martinez
summary: Create an operational protocol that lets PMs and Eng leads hedge capacity across overlapping initiatives by maintaining a rolling runway, running a lightweight internal scope 'auction' to arbitrate contested work, and exposing decision signals to stakeholders and execs.
background: Over the last three cycles we observed repeated mid-cycle scope cuts, last-minute reassignments, and unclear ownership when Dedicated and Private onboarding spikes collided with infrastructure work (runtime performance and autoscaling upgrades). This causes morale issues and delivery slippage. Existing playbooks focus on static tranche reserves; they haven't addressed continuous interleaving of platform and feature work and cross-initiative contention.
proposal: 1) Introduce a 3-week rolling runway buffer per product pillar that is fungible across initiatives but explicitly tagged (platform, onboarding, feature). 2) Implement a lightweight 'scope auction' process at cycle midline: each initiative submits prioritized scope slices with cost in points, PMs vote using a constrained budget to select slices. 3) Add two new dashboards in Console: a capacity heatmap (by role) and a runway consumption tracker displaying committed vs fungible reserves. 4) Formalize escalation to EM/VP level for unresolved auctions.
acceptance_criteria: Runway buffer defined in allocation policy and visible to all contributors
Auction process run in cycle-48 midline with at least 4 participating initiatives
Console dashboard prototype showing runway usage and 80% accuracy against resource calendar
Post-auction retrospective with quantitative metrics (on-time delivery, scope volatility) captured
Stakeholders (Eng leads + PMs) sign off on protocol and escalation path
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (pilot, Cycle 48): run auction for 6 initiatives in infra, dedicated, private, and platform; build read-only dashboard. Phase 2 (Cycle 49): automation of auction form, voting widget in Confluence, dashboard writable by PMs. Phase 3 (Q3): integrate with staffing rota and signal to recruiting for persistent shortfalls.
tradeoffs: Using fungible runway reduces predictability for single initiatives (tradeoff for higher global throughput). The auction introduces process overhead and may favor well-networked PMs; mitigate via anonymized scoring and weighted voting. Building dashboards will divert one full-time engineer from observability work for 3 sprints—risk to current SLO projects.
risks: Auction is gamed by cross-team lobbying
Dashboards show noisy signals leading to overcorrection
Platform spikes (Dedicated onboarding) exceed reserved runway and force emergency reallocation
Inadequate EM/VP engagement could stall escalation decisions
mitigations: Anonymize auction submissions for the vote step, cap per-PM spend, run a two-cycle pilot, and require EM-level pre-approval for runway-draws above threshold. Use smoothing heuristic in dashboard to avoid whipsaw alerts.
decisions_to_make: Size of per-pillar runway (suggested 6% of engineering capacity)
Voting budget per initiative (proportional to committed headcount)
Escalation SLAs and who has veto authority
Visibility rules for dashboard (who can see vs who can act)
